mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_LeastPrivilege lets any caller with any role reach any operation successfully. The injection forces a successful Auditor call to PatchApplicationStatus, which is denied in the permission matrix. The LeastPrivilege assertion checks that every successful operation has a caller with an allowed role, so it will find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.opOutcome = Success and op.opKind = PatchApplicationStatus and Auditor in op.opCaller.roles and not (Officer in op.opCaller.roles) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_NoSelfApproval allows an audit entry where the actor is the same user as the application's applicant, creating a self-approval. The injection forces exactly this configuration on a non-initial entry. Both NoSelfMutation and FR_013_NoSelfApproval check that no such entry exists.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfApprovalViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | some ae.prevStatus and ae.entryActor = ae.entryApplication.appApplicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries allows two distinct audit entries on the same application to share identical prevStatus and newStatus values, which models a duplicated or mutated entry. The injection forces two entries on the same application with the same transition, which both AppendOnly and FR_018_AuditImmutability forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.entryApplication = ae2.entryApplication and ae1.prevStatus = ae2.prevStatus and ae1.newStatus = ae2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuditCompletenessPerApp allows a LoanApplication to exist with no corresponding AuditEntry, breaking the requirement that every application has an initial audit record. The injection forces a LoanApplication with no AuditEntry referencing it.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some app: LoanApplication | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.entryApplication = app }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_ValidationBeforeMutation allows a failed operation to produce audit entries, breaking the invariant that failed requests leave no trace. The injection forces an Operation with Failure outcome that nonetheless has a non-empty opAuditEntries set.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ValidationBeforeMutationViolation { some op: Operation | op.opOutcome = Failure and some op.opAuditEntries }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OwnershipBasedAccess allows a GetApplicationById to succeed for a caller who is neither the application's applicant, nor its assigned officer, nor an auditor — exactly the information-leakage scenario FR-020 and FR-021 forbid. The injection forces such a success for an applicant accessing a different applicant's application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipBasedAccessViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = GetApplicationById and op.opOutcome = Success and (some app: LoanApplication | op.opTarget = app and Applicant in op.opCaller.roles and op.opCaller != app.appApplicant and not (Auditor in op.opCaller.roles) and (no op.opCaller.roles & Officer) ) }
